title: How to play
summary: The in-game guide; each part opens the first time you reach it (first battle, first trait choice, first inventory expansion, first visit to Upgrade).

pages.title: Salvation Breakers
pages.text:
■ Salvation Breakers is a mini game where you merge and upgrade weapons to stop incoming monsters.
■ Efficiently upgrade your characters in the Shop that appears after a wave ends, or through trait selections that appear when leveling up.
■ Except for using Burst Skill, all battles proceed automatically.

pages.title: Salvation Breakers
pages.text:
Waves and Monsters

■ Monsters come in waves, and you must survive a total of 99 waves.
■ Monsters are divided into minions, elites, and bosses. Elites and bosses appear in specific waves.
■ Some minions and elites are special monsters with skills.

pages.title: Shop
pages.text:
Shop

■ The Shop opens after a wave ends.
■ It consists of two sections: Inventory and Weapons.
■ You can manage your inventory or remove unused weapons in the Shop.
■ Drag and drop weapons from the Weapons section into the Inventory to equip them.
■ Weapons placed in the Inventory will be used in battles.
■ When the Shop opens, new weapons will appear in the Weapons section, where you can also store weapons temporarily.
■ Weapons in the Weapons section will disappear when the next wave begins.

pages.title: Shop
pages.text:
Inventory Management

■ Weapons can be freely moved between the Inventory and Weapons sections, as long as their size does not exceed the inventory capacity.
■ Stacking weapons of the same type and rarity will merge them. Merging increases the weapon's rarity and improves its performance.
■ Weapons can be merged in both the Inventory and Weapons sections.

pages.title: Shop
pages.text:
Weapon Types

■ There are two types of weapons: main weapons and sub-weapons.
■ Tap a weapon's icon to view its info.
■ Main weapons attack at regular intervals, dealing damage to monsters.
■ Each main weapon has a tag that determines the traits that apply to that weapon.
■ Sub-weapons cannot attack directly, but they provide buffs that are useful in battle.

pages.title: Shop
pages.text:
Refreshing and Removing Weapons

■ Refreshing will remove all weapons in the Weapons section and replace them with a set number of new weapons.
■ Once all free refreshes are used, refreshing will cost gold.
■ You can also remove unwanted weapons. Removed weapons will no longer appear in the Weapons section.

pages.title: Trait Selection
pages.text:
Trait Selection

■ Defeating monsters grants EXP. Earn a certain amount of EXP to conduct upgrades.
■ When leveling up, you can select traits that provide different effects.
■ Traits are divided into Phase I, II, and III. As the phases increase, higher-phase traits may appear.
■ By default, 3 options are presented, but you can gain an additional option through upgrades.
■ Multiple ordinary traits of the same type can be owned at the same time, while unique traits can only be obtained once per game.

pages.title: Trait Selection
pages.text:
Enhanced Monsters

■ When you have the Enhanced Monsters trait, enhanced monsters may appear in battles.
■ Enhanced monsters have higher HP than ordinary monsters and give additional EXP, gold, and points.
■ This trait helps in getting higher scores.

pages.title: Inventory Expansion
pages.text:
Expanding Your Inventory

■ You can expand your inventory after clearing specific waves.
■ To do so, tap the slots you want to add to your inventory, then tap the Complete Expansion button to confirm.
■ You cannot proceed to the next wave until all Inventory Expansion Points are used.
■ Weapons can be placed in the newly opened slots.

pages.title: Upgrade
pages.text:
Upgrading

■ Defeat monsters to earn gold, which can be used to acquire useful skills for your characters.
■ Use the Reset button to get back spent gold and reset skill levels.
